newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan share turnover perks up, index down again.
newsitem.headline: Jordan share turnover perks up, index down again.

text.p: Turnover on the Amman stock exchange picked up slightly on Tuesday from Monday's eight-month low but the official bourse index slipped another 0.05 percent.
Shares worth 426,000 dinars ($602,000) changed hands, up from 202,000 dinars on Monday.
"The turnover's a little better but prices are still down," said one broker.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.07 points to 147.67 points, its eighth consecutive daily fall.

The exchange, blighted by high domestic interest rates and worries over barriers to trade with sanction-hit Iraq to the east and with Israel and the Palestinian territories to the west, has traded in a tight range since early October.
"There were no changes today, nothing new," said one trader.
Blue-chip Arab Bank Group accounted for the largest turnover, worth nearly 50,000 dinars, but fell 0.5 dinars to close at 246 dinars.
But two other leading banks, Industrial Development Bank and Housing Bank, rose in moderate trade to cushion the index fall.
Industrial Development Bank rose 0.05 dinars to 2.27 dinars in trade worth 38,000 dinars and Housing Bank rose 0.07 dinars to 4.90 dinars after 3,300 shares changed hands.
Overall, declining shares outnumbered gainers by 20 to nine, while 14 traded but closed unchanged.
The Pearl Investable Index of the AFM's 45 soundest and most frequently traded shares fell 0.12 percent to 80.38 points from 80.48 on Monday, 15.84 percent down from the same time last year.
